messages.subject: Senior Backend Engineer at Larkspur Robotics (Pittsburgh, hybrid)
messages.body:
Hi there,

I'm a technical recruiter at Sterling & Vane Talent, and I'm working with Larkspur Robotics on a Senior Backend Engineer hire for their fleet-management platform. They're building the software that coordinates a few hundred warehouse robots in real time: Go services, Postgres, and a lot of event streaming.

Your background on high-throughput APIs looked like a strong match. The role is hybrid (three days a week in their Pittsburgh office), with a base range of $175-195k plus equity.

Would you be open to a 20-minute call this week or next? Happy to share the full job description first if that's easier.

Best,
Owen Fairbanks
Senior Technical Recruiter, Sterling & Vane Talent

messages.subject: Staff Data Engineer opportunity with a leading bank
messages.body: Hi, I hope you're well. I'm Hye-jin, a recruiter with Northbeam Search Partners. I'm partnering with a well-established bank in Chicago that is modernizing its data platform and is hiring a Staff Data Engineer to lead the migration from on-prem Hadoop to a lakehouse architecture. Given your experience with dbt and Spark, I think you'd be a great fit. Are you open to hearing more? Compensation is up to $230k base plus bonus.

messages.subject: Re: Staff Data Engineer opportunity with a leading bank
messages.body:
Thanks for getting back to me so quickly! To answer your question: the client is Quillfeather Bank. The team is about 18 engineers, reporting to the Head of Data Platform. It's hybrid, two days a week downtown.

> On Nov 5, 2025, you wrote:
> Thanks Hye-jin, I might be open to it. Which bank is it, and is it remote-friendly?

I've attached the full description. If it looks interesting, could you send me an updated resume and a couple of times for a quick screen?

messages.subject: Re: Staff Data Engineer opportunity with a leading bank
messages.body: Great speaking with you today. As agreed, I've submitted your profile to Quillfeather Bank's hiring team for the Staff Data Engineer role, and I'll let you know as soon as I hear back about a first-round interview. It usually takes about a week. In the meantime, if anything changes on your side (another process moving faster, a change in your availability), just let me know so I can keep them updated.

They need someone to own their Terraform and Kubernetes setup while the permanent platform team is being hired. It's fully remote within the US, $95-110/hour on W2 or corp-to-corp, and the start date is flexible within the next month.

If you or anyone you know might be interested, reply here and I'll send over the details and next steps.

I'm leading a confidential search for an Engineering Manager to run a payments team of seven at a Series B fintech in Austin. The company processes several billion dollars a year for independent pharmacies and just closed a $60M round. They can't be named publicly yet, but I can share more on a call.

You'd own ingestion of satellite, flood, and wildfire datasets and work directly with me and our two data scientists. We're 11 people, seed-funded, remote-first with a small office in Denver. Salary is $170-190k plus meaningful equity.

Demand is concentrated in platform, security, and ML infrastructure roles, while frontend and generalist openings remain flat. Senior candidates report more recruiter outreach but longer processes.

2. Deep dive: when event-driven workers beat cron. We walk through a real migration and the three mistakes that cost a team two months.

3. Sponsored: Tracepoint Observability cuts log costs by up to 40%. Start a free trial.

Thanks for reading. Forward this to a friend, or unsubscribe at any time.
